messages:
maya: bringing up flan-7b-q8 on the eval harness — seeing tokenization oddities + batch-response misalignment. CI runner job failed too. anyone seen prompt_id<>response mapping issues? :eyes:

maya: reproducer command i used:
```
python -m scripts/run_eval --model flan-7b-q8 --dataset vicuna-dev --batch-size 8 --shuffle True
pytest tests/eval_runner_test.py::test_batch_alignment -k flan
```

maya: tail of the failing log:
```
E AssertionError: response mismatch
expected prompt_id=42 got response for prompt_id=7
File "/repo/eval_runner.py", line 243, in _align_batches
    out = outputs[index_map]
```

ryan: hmm, that stack looks like the index map is stale after quantized model warmup. do you have the seed + full log?

maya: full log attached to CI (job 9876) but pasted critical part above. seed=2025-11-03T09:12Z. also noticed token counts differ between hf tokenizer and our cached tokenizer mapping (off by 1 for long prompts).

anika: two quick things to check: 1) tokenizer special tokens (pad/eos) not present -> can shift offsets, 2) runner shuffling + async kvcache flush can reorder outputs if we don't pin request ids. try `--shuffle False` to confirm.

sam: quantization shouldn't change tokenization but it can change timing, which exposes race conditions in the runner. suspect `_align_batches` assumes outputs order equals request order. we had a similar flakiness in 2024 with batcher refactor.

ryan: can you run this small repro locally with debug logging?
```
python -m scripts/run_eval --model flan-7b-q8 --dataset vicuna-dev --batch-size 4 --shuffle False --log-level debug --dump-request-ids /tmp/ids.json
```

maya: ran that, dump shows request ids: [10,11,12,13] but outputs mapped to [12,10,13,11]. index_map = [2,0,3,1] printed from runner. patch idea: use explicit request_id in response envelope and align by id not array position.

anika: agreed. also for tokenizer: add missing pad token to HF tokenizer before saving mapping:
```
if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
    tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"pad_token": "<pad>"})
```

ci-bot: Job failed: CI/eval/runner-flan-q8 (job 9876) — see https://ci.redwood.ai/9876 :bug:

eval-bot: flaky-test-detection: test_batch_alignment failed 3 times in the last 24h (likely race). :rotating_light:

maya: quick hotfix pushed in branch `fix/eval-align-by-id`: change _align_batches to align by response['request_id'] and stop shuffling request index list when computing alignment. small unit test added.

sam: nice. can you also add a regression test that simulates delayed output ordering? looks like we never mocked out out-of-order responses.

maya: adding test now — `tests/test_alignment_out_of_order.py` with synthetic runner that returns permuted outputs. CI run triggered.

ryan: :thumbsup: please link PR. after CI green we should backport to 0.18.x (Dedicated infra still on that runtime).

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval/compare/fix/eval-align-by-id — CI currently running. thanks all. :shipit:
